Part 1 · Fundamentals

What sets the pressure, temperature and power of a gas compressor?

Part 1 · outline

Five pieces of physics the simulator solves

  2. Polytropic compressionoutlet temperature, head and power

Part 1 · the gas

One number describes how this gas heats when squeezed

$M$
molar mass of the export gas (CH₄ 74 %, CO₂ 12 %, assumed analysis)
22.275 kg/kmol
$\bar c_p$
ideal-gas molar heat capacity
40.53 J/(mol·K)
$R_u$
universal gas constant
8.314 J/(mol·K)
$\gamma$
heat capacity ratio $c_p/c_v$
–
$R$
specific gas constant $R_u/M$
J/(kg·K)
$\gamma=\dfrac{\bar c_p}{\bar c_p-R_u}=\dfrac{40.53}{40.53-8.314}=1.258$

$R=8314/22.275=373.3$ J/(kg·K); $c_p=1819.5$ J/(kg·K)

Air has γ = 1.40; heavier gases approach 1.0

Part 1 · the gas

At 30–120 bar the gas is not ideal: Z corrects it

$Z$
compressibility factor; the model's fit for this gas
–
$P,\ T$
absolute pressure, absolute temperature
bar a, K
$\rho$
gas density
kg/m³
$a$
speed of sound in the gas
m/s
$Z=1-\left(0.0027P-8.9\times10^{-6}P^2\right)\left(\dfrac{310}{T}\right)^2$
$\rho=\dfrac{P}{ZRT}\qquad a=\sqrt{\gamma ZRT}$

Z ≈ 0.92 in V-101, 0.87 in V-102, 0.81 in the discharge header

Interactive · the model's own Z, ρ and a

Density doubles between the sections; sound slows a little

From the previous slide$\rho=\dfrac{P}{ZRT}\qquad a=\sqrt{\gamma ZRT}$

From V-101 (31 bar a) to V-102 (61 bar a) the density rises from 29 to 60 kg/m³: section 2 handles half the volume, so it is a smaller machine.

Part 1 · polytropic compression

From the compression path to the outlet temperature step 1 of 2

The gas properties are fixed. Next: what one section does to that gas.
$r$
pressure ratio of one section, $P_2/P_1$
–
$E_p$
polytropic efficiency of the section
–
$n,\ m$
polytropic exponent; $m=(n-1)/n$
–
$Pv^{\,n}=\text{const}$a real compressor follows a polytropic path
$\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}=r^{(n-1)/n}=r^{m}$combine the path with $Pv=ZRT$, Z nearly constant
$m=\dfrac{\gamma-1}{\gamma E_p}$losses heat the gas: lower $E_p$, larger $m$

Part 1 · polytropic compression

From the outlet temperature to head and power step 2 of 2

$H_p$
polytropic head: useful work per kilogram
J/kg
$\dot m$
mass flow through the section
kg/s
$\dot W$
gas power absorbed by the section
W
$H_p=\dfrac{RT_1\left(r^{m}-1\right)}{m}$integrate $v\,dP$ along the polytropic path
$\dfrac{H_p}{E_p}=c_p\,(T_2-T_1)$all shaft work ends as gas enthalpy
$\dot W=\dot m\,c_p\,(T_2-T_1)$multiply by the mass flow

Ideal-gas form, as the simulator uses; real-gas Z̄ lowers head by ≈ 8–13 % (Design tab)

Part 1 · polytropic compression

Section 1 at design, by hand

From the last two slides$T_2=T_1r^{m}\qquad m=\dfrac{\gamma-1}{\gamma E_p}\qquad \dot W=\dot m\,c_p\,(T_2-T_1)$
$r=\dfrac{61.91}{31.01}=1.996$nozzle 61.9 bar a over suction 31.0 bar a
$m=\dfrac{0.258}{1.258\times0.685}=0.2995$$E_p$ = 0.685 for section 1
$T_2=308.15\times1.996^{0.2995}=379.0\ \text{K}=105.9\ \text{°C}$suction 35 °C
$\dot W=61.75\times1819.5\times70.9=7.96\ \text{MW}$same answer as the simulator

Ratio, efficiency and suction temperature set the outlet

Polytropic section$T_2=T_1r^{m}\qquad m=\dfrac{\gamma-1}{\gamma E_p}$

At the overall ratio 3.96 one section would reach ≈ 192 °C: above the 150 °C seal ceiling, so K-100 needs two sections.

Part 1 · the compressor map

A map turns speed and flow into head

The lecture relations give the head a ratio needs. The map gives the head a section can make.
$N'$
speed as a fraction of 9 500 rpm
–
$Q_d,\ H_d$
design suction flow and head
m³/s, J/kg
$q$
flow coefficient, $(Q/Q_d)/N'$
–
$\psi$
head coefficient, $H_p/(H_dN'^2)$
–
$\psi(q)=1.16-0.16\left(\dfrac{q-0.40}{0.60}\right)^2$

peak head at low flow; ψ = 1 at the design point q = 1

Head ∝ speed², flow ∝ speed (fan laws)

Interactive · the model's psiOf, mthOf and stageSolve

Where section 1 runs for a given speed and ratio

The map$H_p=\psi(q)\,H_d\,N'^2$

At fixed speed a higher ratio pushes the point left toward surge; only more speed lifts the curve and buys back the margin.

Part 1 · the compressor map

Two walls bound every speed line

Surge (minimum flow)

Past peak head, at $q_s=0.62$, the section cannot hold the pressure behind it: flow reverses, the machine thumps and heats.

Stonewall (maximum flow)

Gas in the impeller throat reaches sound speed; head and efficiency collapse.

$\text{margin}=\left(\dfrac{q}{q_s}-1\right)\times100\%$
$M_{th}=0.74\,q\,N'^{0.3}\,\dfrac{a_d}{a}$

$M_{th}$ throat Mach number; $a_d$ design speed of sound, 365.6 m/s. Design: margin 61 %, $M_{th}$ 0.74.

Part 1 · choked flow

Below a critical pressure ratio, valve flow stops responding downstream

$P_0,\ T_0$
upstream pressure and temperature
bar a, K
$P_2$
downstream pressure
bar a
$C_dA$
effective valve flow area
m²
$G^*$
critical (sonic) mass flux
kg/(m²·s)
$\dfrac{P_2}{P_0}\le\left(\dfrac{2}{\gamma+1}\right)^{\frac{\gamma}{\gamma-1}}=0.553$
$\dot m=C_dA\,G^*=C_dA\,P_0\sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma}{ZRT_0}}\left(\dfrac{2}{\gamma+1}\right)^{\frac{\gamma+1}{2(\gamma-1)}}$

UV-103, UV-108, PV-102, the BDVs and HV-101/102 all work this way

Interactive · the model's nozzle() with the UV-103 area

Recycle flow through a wide-open UV-103

Choked when$P_2/P_0\le0.553$

UV-103 works at $P_2/P_0$ ≈ 0.50, already choked: its flow follows the interstage pressure, not the suction pressure.

Part 1 · coolers

E-101 and E-102 are counter-flow coolers rated by ε-NTU

$C$
heat capacity rate $\dot m c_p$ of one stream
W/K
$C_r$
$C_{min}/C_{max}$
–
$UA$
overall conductance (installed)
W/K
$\varepsilon$
effectiveness: duty over the largest possible duty
–
$\varepsilon=\dfrac{1-e^{-NTU(1-C_r)}}{1-C_re^{-NTU(1-C_r)}},\quad NTU=\dfrac{UA}{C_{min}}$
$\dot Q=\varepsilon\,C_{min}\,(T_{gas,in}-T_{cm})$

E-101: UA 394 kW/K; TV-106 sets the cooling-medium flow

Interactive · ε-NTU exactly as the model's E-101

How the cooling-medium valve sets the gas outlet temperature

Cooler duty$\dot Q=\varepsilon\,C_{min}\,(T_{gas,in}-T_{cm})$

Near 55 % open E-101 gives 40 °C; wide open ≈ 35.5 °C. The curve flattens as the valve opens, so extra opening buys little cooling.

The gas turbine loses power on a hot day

MW
$T_{amb}$

°C
$\dot m_f$

kg/s

35.8 MJ/kg
$\dot W_{av}=22\,\text{MW}\,\left[1-0.0065\,(T_{amb}-15)\right]$

At 30 °C: 19.86 MW available; 16.70 MW load burns 1.38 kg/s

Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • γ = 1.258 and Z (0.92 → 0.81) describe the gas; density doubles between sections.
  • $T_2=T_1r^m$ and $\dot W=\dot m c_p(T_2-T_1)$ give 105.9 °C and 7.96 MW for section 1.
  • The map sets the head a section can make; surge at q 0.62, stonewall when the throat goes sonic.
  • Recycle, flare and blowdown valves are choked: flow follows upstream pressure.
  • ε-NTU sets the cooler outlets; GT-100 has 19.86 MW at 30 °C.

Part 2 · Design approach

How was K-100 sized from its design basis?

Part 2 · outline

Six design decisions, in the order an engineer makes them

  1. Design basis and machine typeflow, pressures and why a centrifugal machine
  2. Number of sectionswhy one section is not enough and two are
  3. Interstage pressure and intercoolingequal ratios and the power they save
  4. The driverwhy a gas turbine, and how much margin it has
  5. Coolers, anti-surge valves and blowdownequipment sized with deliberate margins

Part 2 · design basis

What K-100 must do (teaching basis, assumed)

QuantityDesign
Production gas200 MMSCFD = 61.75 kg/s
Suction V-10130.0 barg, 35 °C
Pipeline inlet≈ 120 barg
Onshore arrival70 barg
Air · cooling medium30 °C · 30 °C
The pipeline friction sets the export pressure: 70 barg must still arrive onshore after several hundred kilometres.

Part 2 · machine type

A large volume flow at high pressure: a centrifugal compressor

Part 1$Q=\dot m/\rho=61.75/29.2=2.116\ \text{m}^3/\text{s}\ (4\,480\ \text{ACFM})$

Volume

Thousands of ACFM sit in the centrifugal band of the lecture's selection chart.

Ratio per section

A centrifugal section makes about 1.7–2.0 before tip speed and Mach limit it.

Speed

9 500 rpm suits a direct gas-turbine drive with no gearbox.

Part 2 · number of sections

One section is too hot; two sections at equal ratio fit

Part 1 and the lecture rule for N sections$T_2=T_1r^{m}\qquad r=\left(\dfrac{P_{out}}{P_{in}}\right)^{1/N}$
$r_{total}=122.8/31.01=3.96$section 2 nozzle over suction, bar a
$N=1:\ T_2=308.15\times3.96^{0.2995}-273.15=192\ \text{°C}$above the 150 °C seal ceiling
$N=2:\ r=3.96^{1/2}=1.99,\ T_2=106\ \text{and}\ 116\ \text{°C}$within 2.0 per section and below 150 °C

Interactive · lecture method, Ep from the lecture chart per section

Try one to four sections with intercooling

Two intercooled sections save ≈ 1.3 MW (7 %) against one hot section; a third saves only ≈ 0.4 MW more for another cooler and scrubber.

Part 2 · interstage pressure

Equal ratios put the interstage at the geometric mean

$P_i=\sqrt{P_1P_3}=\sqrt{31.01\times122.8}=61.7\ \text{bar a}$

$P_1$ suction, $P_3$ final discharge, $P_i$ interstage (bar a)

  • Intercooled back near $T_1$, both sections then do almost equal work.
  • Design: 61.9 bar a at the section 1 nozzle, 61.4 bar a in V-102.
  • Section 2 still works harder: warmer suction (40 °C) and lower $E_p$.

Interactive · both sections, lecture relations

Move the interstage pressure and watch the total power

Each section$\dot W=\dot m\,c_p\,T_1\left(r^{m}-1\right)$

The total is flat near the minimum (≈ 62.8 bar a): a few bar either way costs only kilowatts, so equal ratios are good enough.

Part 2 · the driver

16.7 MW at 9 500 rpm calls for a gas turbine

The machine is sized. Next: what turns it.
Part 1$\dot W_{av}=22\,\text{MW}\left[1-0.0065\,(T_{amb}-15)\right]$
CheckValueVerdict
Shaft power at design16.70 MWfar above motor range
GT-100 available at 30 °C19.86 MWmargin 3.16 MW
Air temperature for zero margin52 °Chot days cost margin

Interactive · 112 steady model runs, 3 000 s each

Shaft power needed against GT-100 available power

At 30 °C the turbine limits only above ≈ 110 % production; at 45 °C from ≈ 105 %. Beyond the limit, suction rises and the excess is flared.

Part 2 · coolers

E-101 and E-102 are built 50 % larger than the clean duty needs

E-101E-102
Duty at design7.3 MW7.7 MW
Clean $UA$ → installed263 → 394 kW/K216 → 324 kW/K
Valve at designTV-106 55 %TV-111 49 %

Margin covers fouling and warm cooling medium: E-101 still holds 40 °C up to a 35 °C supply (model runs).

Part 2 · anti-surge valves and blowdown

Valves sized on choked flow

Part 1$\dot m=C_dA\,G^*(P_0,T_0)$

UV-103 · UV-108

$C_dA$ 77.8 and 37.2 cm²: 1.6 × design flow when choked, so recycle alone can protect at any speed.

BDV-101 · BDV-112

45 mm restriction orifices empty the loop to 6.9 barg in ≈ 6 min; API 521 asks ≤ 15 min.

Interactive · seven ESD-2 runs of the model

Choose the restriction orifice size

A larger orifice empties faster but loads the flare harder: 45 mm meets 15 minutes with margin at ≈ 300 t/h peak.

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • 2.1 m³/s at 30 → 120 barg: a centrifugal machine at 9 500 rpm.
  • Ratio 3.96 needs two sections (r ≈ 2.0 each); one would reach 192 °C.
  • Interstage near √(P₁P₃) with intercooling to 40 °C; the optimum is flat.
  • GT-100: 19.86 MW at 30 °C against 16.70 MW needed.
  • Coolers carry 50 % UA margin; UV and BDV valves are sized on choked flow.

Part 3 · Operation approach

How is K-100 started, run, turned down and stopped safely?

Part 3 · outline

The operating life of K-100 in five stages

  1. States of the unitTRIPPED, READY, START and RUN, and what moves between them
  2. Cold start-uputilities, pressurising, the turbine start and loading
  3. Normal runningthe suction-pressure-to-speed cascade
  4. Turndownspeed first, then anti-surge recycle
  5. StoppingESD-1 and settle-out, ESD-2 and blowdown

Part 3 · states

The safety system decides which state the unit is in

TRIPPEDreset →READYstart →START69.5 % speed →RUN

TRIPPED

ESDVs shut, fuel off, recycle fully open.

READY

Latch reset; ESDV-101 may open.

START

Crank 30 s, ignite 10 s, accelerate.

RUN

At 69.5 % speed SIC-100 goes to AUTO at 70 %.

Interactive · the graded start-up, step by step

Cold start-up of K-100 in eight steps

Each step clears one condition the next step needs: the turbine will not even crank until all seven start permissives are met.

Part 3 · start-up

The seven GT-100 start permissives

PermissiveWhy
SIS reset (READY)no trip latched
Lube oil PI-150 ≥ 2.0 bargbearings fed before turning
P-160 cooling medium runningcoolers ready
ESDV-101 open, PI-101 ≥ 20 barggas in the loop
UV-103 and UV-108 ≥ 90 %start on full recycle
Scrubber levels below 60 %no liquid to impellers
BDVs closedloop not venting

Part 3 · start-up

HV-101 fills the loop slowly through a choked nozzle

Part 1$\dot m=C_dA\,G^*(P_0,T_0)\quad\text{while}\quad P_2/P_0\le0.553$
  • From 3 barg the bypass is choked: flow depends on header pressure only.
  • Keep the rise below 8 bar/min: fast filling heats the gas and stresses seals.
  • ESDV-101 opens only when the pressure difference is below 3 bar.

Part 3 · normal running

Suction pressure is held by speed, through a cascade

Once loaded, the operator leaves two loops in series to take whatever gas arrives.
$SP_{SIC}=70+0.35\,OUT_{PIC}\ \ (\%)$

PIC-101 output 0–100 % maps to a speed set point 70–105 %

  • More gas arrives → V-101 pressure rises → PIC-101 asks for more speed.
  • SIC-100 opens FV-100; GT-100 burns more fuel; the shaft accelerates.
  • The faster machine draws more gas and pressure returns to 30 barg.

Interactive · model run, PIC-101 set point step at t = 10 s

A one-bar set-point change, followed through the cascade

Cascade$SP_{SIC}=70+0.35\,OUT_{PIC}$

PIC-101 never moves a valve itself: it moves the speed set point, the speed loop moves the fuel, and power follows the speed.

Part 3 · turndown

Less gas: slow down first, recycle only when you must

Part 1$\text{margin}=\left(\dfrac{q}{0.62}-1\right)\times100\%$

Speed

The cascade slows the machine; the pipeline still needs head, so q falls toward surge.

Recycle

At the 10 % control line UIC-103/108 open UV-103/108; recycled gas costs fuel.

Fast opening

Below 5 % margin the valve steps open quickly, before the flow reverses.

Interactive · steady model runs at 30 °C air

Production against speed, surge margin and recycle

Speed alone carries the turndown to ≈ 60 % production; below that the margin sits on the 10 % control line and UV-103 recycles.

Interactive · model run: production cut to 40 % at t = 20 s

Section 1 on its map while the gas falls away

The margin dips to ≈ 3 %, the fast opening throws UV-103 to ≈ 68 % and no surge occurs; then the valve settles near the control line.

Part 3 · stopping

Two ways to stop: settle out or blow down

ESD-1 (process shutdown)

Fuel and ESDVs shut, recycle opens; gas settles near 69.5 barg. Vent with HV-102 before restart.

ESD-2 (with blowdown)

Adds BDV-101/112 and shuts the wells: the loop empties to flare.

Lube oil runs until the train stops.

Interactive · model runs from design, button pressed at t = 10 s

Pressures in the loop after ESD-1 or ESD-2

ESD-1 equalises suction, interstage and discharge near 69.5 barg; ESD-2 brings both sides below 6.9 barg in about six minutes.

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • The SIS state machine runs TRIPPED → READY → START → RUN.
  • Start-up: utilities, reset, pressurise (ΔP < 3 bar), start on full recycle, load in cascade.
  • PIC-101 holds suction by moving the speed set point.
  • Turndown uses speed first; recycle holds the 10 % control line.
  • ESD-1 settles out near 69.5 barg; ESD-2 blows down to 6.9 barg in ≈ 6 min.

Interactive · click a stream number

The export compression unit and its streams

Fourteen streams describe the whole unit: one gas path (1–8), five side streams and the flare header (13).

Part 4 · main gas path

Inlet: from the separator to V-101 (streams 1–2)

The diagram gives the map. Now walk it, stream by stream.
  • FI-001 meters 200 MMSCFD of well gas.
  • PIC-102 flares through PV-102 above 32 barg.
  • ESDV-101, with bypass HV-101, isolates the compressor loop.
  • V-101 catches liquid (0.8 t/h) before it can reach an impeller.

Header protection: PSHH-001 at 34.5 barg shuts the wells; PSV-001 lifts at 36 barg.

Part 4 · summary

What Part 4 settled

  • Streams 1–8 are the gas path; 9–14 are fuel, liquids, recycles and flare.
  • Pressure rises 30 → 61 → 122 barg; temperature saws 34 → 105 → 40 → 116 → 45 °C.
  • Recycles return cooled gas; all relief goes to one flare header.
  • Mass, energy and shaft power balances close at design.

The inner loop is about eight times faster than the outer one, as a cascade needs.

Part 5 · anti-surge control

Each section has its own anti-surge loop on its own flow element

The cascade keeps the pressure. Two more loops keep each section out of surge.
Part 1$\text{margin}=\left(\dfrac{q}{q_s}-1\right)\times100\%,\quad q_s=0.62$
  • FT-103 and FT-108 measure each section's suction flow; with P and T the controller computes q.
  • Set point 10 %: the control line, safely right of surge.
  • Recycle is taken after a cooler, so recycled gas never heats the suction.

Interactive · UIC-103 action at each margin

What the anti-surge controller does at a given margin

Above 10 % the valve stays shut; between 5 and 10 % the PI loop opens it; below 5 % it steps open at 60 %/s.

Interactive · normal design positions against loss of instrument air

Every valve is chosen to fail to the safe side

With no air the machine loses fuel, recycles, flares and blows down: it stops in the safe state on its own.

Part 5 · safety system

Two trip levels, independent of the DCS

I-1 · compressor trip (PSD)

Fuel and both ESDVs shut; recycle opens fully; PV-102 jumps to ≥ 80 %.

I-2 · ESD-2 with blowdown

Everything in I-1, plus BDV-101/112 open and XV-001 shuts the wells.

Upstream, PSHH-001 (34.5 barg) shuts XV-001; PSV-001 (36 barg) is the last layer.

Interactive · from the model's tripConditions and bmsTrip

Pick a cause: see its set point, delay and effects

Every I-1 cause has the same effects; only ESD-2 adds blowdown and well shut-in.

Part 5 · safety system

After a trip: three conditions before a restart

Reset

Allowed only with no trip cause standing and the train below 5 % speed.

Equalise

ESDV-101 opens only with less than 3 bar across it: vent with HV-102 or fill with HV-101.

Permissives

All seven start permissives green, including full recycle.

Part 5 · summary

What Part 5 settled

  • Eleven loops: pressure, speed, two anti-surge, two temperatures, two levels, flare, two hand valves.
  • PIC-101 is the master of a speed cascade; SIC-100 moves the fuel valve.
  • Each section's own anti-surge loop holds a 10 % margin; fast opening below 5 %.
  • Valves fail to the safe side; I-1 stops the machine, I-2 also blows it down.

Part 7 · Other unit operations

What do the scrubbers, coolers, turbine, utilities and pipeline around K-100 do?

Part 7 · outline

Six units that make the compressor work

  1. Scrubbers V-101 and V-102Souders–Brown sizing and liquid hold-up
  2. Coolers and the cooling-medium pumpE-101, E-102 and P-160
  3. Gas turbine GT-100available power, fuel and exhaust
  4. Lube oilmain and standby pumps and their protection
  5. Flare system and export pipelinerelief paths and the pressure the pipeline demands

Part 7 · scrubbers

A scrubber is sized so droplets fall faster than the gas rises

$u_{max}$
highest allowed upward gas velocity
m/s
$K$
Souders–Brown factor for a mesh pad (assumed)
0.09 m/s
$\rho_L,\ \rho_G$
liquid and gas densities
kg/m³
$D$
minimum vessel diameter
m
$u_{max}=K\sqrt{\dfrac{\rho_L-\rho_G}{\rho_G}}$
$D=\sqrt{\dfrac{4Q}{\pi\,u_{max}}}$

V-101: 2.41 m → 2.5 m chosen; V-102: 2.15 m → 2.2 m (Design tab)

Interactive · model densities, Souders–Brown

How big must V-101 and V-102 be?

Souders–Brown$u_{max}=K\sqrt{(\rho_L-\rho_G)/\rho_G}$

V-102 is smaller than V-101 although it carries the same gas: at twice the pressure the gas is denser and its volume halves.

Part 7 · scrubbers

Levels: controlled at 40 %, tripped at 85 %

V-101V-102
Normal liquid inflow0.8 t/h0.4 t/h
Controller · valve (fails)LIC-101 · LV-101 (FC)LIC-107 · LV-107 (FC)
Time from 40 % to 85 %, valve shut≈ 54 min≈ 66 min
TripLSHH-101LSHH-107

Part 7 · coolers

One cooling-medium pump serves both coolers

E-101 intercooler

7.3 MW, 105 → 40 °C. Cooler suction gas saves section 2 power but condenses more liquid.

E-102 aftercooler

7.7 MW, 116 → 45 °C, for the pipeline coating.

P-160

Cooling medium at 30 °C; return ≈ 75 °C at design.

Both valves fail open: loss of air gives full cooling, never none

Part 7 · gas turbine

GT-100: a two-shaft industrial gas turbine on the compressor shaft

The scrubbers and coolers condition the gas. The turbine supplies the work.
Part 1$\dot W_{av}=22\,\text{MW}\left[1-0.0065\,(T_{amb}-15)\right]\qquad \dot m_f=\dfrac{\dot W+3.06\ \text{MW}}{0.40\ \text{LHV}}$
  • Rated 22 MW at ISO; burns gas from V-102.
  • Thermal efficiency ≈ 34 % at design; the rest leaves as exhaust heat.
  • Exhaust temperature rises with load and with air temperature.

Interactive · the model's GT-100 relations

Air temperature, load, fuel and exhaust

Every 10 °C of air costs ≈ 1.4 MW: at 45 °C the turbine gives 17.7 MW, barely above the design load.

Part 7 · lube oil

Oil before rotation, oil until rest

P-150A mainheader ≈ 3.0 bargP-150B standbytripPSLL-150 1.2 barg
  • Start permissive: PI-150 at least 2.0 barg.
  • P-150B is the standby pump: it starts automatically on low oil pressure.
  • After a stop the train coasts for several minutes: keep oil running until it rests.

Part 7 · flare system

Four routes to one flare header

RouteOpens whenFrom
PV-102header above 32 bargproduction header
PSV-001header at 36 bargproduction header
BDV-101 · BDV-112ESD-2suction · discharge
HV-102operator ventingV-101

All choked; blowdown gas reaches ≈ −21 °C (model run), so the flare line needs low-temperature steel

Part 7 · export pipeline

The pipeline sets the discharge pressure

$P_{in}$
pipeline inlet pressure
bar a
$P_{arr}$
onshore arrival pressure
bar a
$\dot m$
export mass flow
kg/s
$K_w$
line coefficient, fitted at design
bar²·s²/kg²
$P_{in}^2-P_{arr}^2=K_w\,\dot m^2$

Weymouth-type line; $K_w$ = 2.66 from 121.3 and 71.0 bar a at 60.3 kg/s

450 m³ of line packing: pressures move over ≈ 10 minutes

Interactive · the model's pipeline relation

Export flow and arrival pressure set the discharge

Pipeline$P_{in}=\sqrt{P_{arr}^2+K_w\dot m^2}$

More export needs a higher inlet pressure, and so does a higher arrival pressure: the margin to PSHH-112 shrinks either way.

Part 7 · summary

What Part 7 settled

  • Scrubbers are sized by Souders–Brown; ≈ 1 h of hold-up below LSHH.
  • P-160 cools both coolers; their valves fail open.
  • GT-100 loses ≈ 0.14 MW per °C of air; fuel ≈ 2 % of production.
  • Lube oil runs before the start and until the train rests.
  • Four relief routes share one flare; the pipeline relation sets the discharge pressure.

Part 8 · grading

A procedure is worth 10 points, but safety comes first

Unsafe: 0

Surge, a discharge above 140 °C, turning without lube oil, an unplanned trip.

Deductions

Order not followed −4; over the time limit −2; no communication −1.

Live grading

The optimisation scores 2.5 per target met after 60 minutes.

Part 8 · graded procedure

Cold start-up of K-100 from a depressurised loop

Objective. Bring K-100 from a depressurised, stopped loop to full export without surge, overheating or flaring, in the right order.
Situation. The loop is depressurised to 3 barg after maintenance; everything is stopped. The wells produce 100 MMSCFD to flare through PV-102. Start the utilities, pressurise, start GT-100 on full recycle, load the machine and stop the flaring.
Start: cold, depressurisedTime limit: 3 hgraded on the tracker

Tracker steps

  1. Lube oil: P-150A running and PI-150 ≥ 2.5 barg
  2. Cooling medium: P-160 running, TIC-106 and TIC-111 in AUTO
  3. SIS reset (READY)
  4. Loop pressurised with HV-101: PIC-101 ≥ 28 barg
  5. ESDV-101 open and HV-101 closed (≤ 2 %)
  6. GT-100 started on full recycle: unit in RUN at ≥ 69.5 % speed
  7. Anti-surge UIC-103 and UIC-108 in AUTO, LIC-101 and LIC-107 in AUTO
  8. ESDV-113 open
  9. Loaded: PIC-101 in AUTO at 30.0 ± 0.3 barg and SIC-100 in cascade
  10. Hold 10 min: flare < 1 t/h, suction 29–31 barg, margins ≥ 7 %, export ≥ 180 MMSCFD

Part 8 · graded procedure

Normal shutdown and vent to header pressure

Objective. Stop K-100 as planned with the least flaring, leaving the loop at header pressure and the lube oil running.
Situation. Planned stop for a borescope inspection with no flaring. Ask production control to shut in the wells, let the machine run down to minimum speed on the anti-surge valves, stop it with ESD-1, keep the lube oil on and vent the settled-out loop to header pressure.
Start: lined out at designTime limit: 1 hgraded on the tracker

Tracker steps

  1. Production control has shut in the wells: FI-001 below 10 MMSCFD (Field tab, telephone)
  2. SIC-100 out of cascade (AUTO), speed ≤ 72 %, anti-surge valves in AUTO
  3. Compressor stopped with ESD-1 (PSD)
  4. Train at rest: speed < 1 %
  5. Lube oil still running (P-150A or P-150B)
  6. Loop vented with HV-102 to within 3 bar of the header
  7. HV-102 closed

Part 8 · graded procedure

Emergency shutdown with blowdown

Objective. Respond to an emergency order at once: shut down with blowdown and confirm the loop empties within 15 minutes.
Situation. Unit at design. An emergency order will arrive.
Start: lined out at designTime limit: 30 mingraded on the tracker

Tracker steps

  1. ESD-2 pressed within 60 s of the order
  2. ESDV-101, ESDV-113 and XV-001 shut; BDV-101/112 open
  3. Lube oil kept running during the rundown
  4. Loop depressurised to ≤ 6.9 barg (API 521: within 15 min)

Part 8 · graded procedure

GT-100 trip: vent, restart and reload

Objective. Recover from a driver trip: keep the flare in control, vent the settled-out loop, restart and reload.
Situation. Unit at design. Stand by.
Start: lined out at designTime limit: 2 hgraded on the tracker

Tracker steps

  1. K-100 trip alarm acknowledged
  2. Flare in control: PIC-102 in AUTO, header below 33 barg
  3. Loop vented with HV-102 to within 3 bar of the header
  4. SIS reset after the GT fault is cleared
  5. ESDV-101 open and HV-102 closed
  6. GT-100 restarted (RUN), UIC-103/108 in AUTO, ESDV-113 open
  7. PIC-101 in AUTO at 30 barg and SIC-100 in cascade
  8. Hold 10 min: flare < 1 t/h, suction 29–31 barg, margins ≥ 7 %

Part 8 · graded procedure

Unknown upset: find it and keep the compressor running

Objective. Find an unannounced upset, remove its cause and keep the compressor running without a trip.
Situation. Unit at design. Something will happen. Find it and keep the machine running.
Start: lined out at designTime limit: 1 hgraded on the tracker

Tracker steps

  1. New alarms acknowledged within 60 s
  2. Cause found and removed without a trip
  3. Affected controllers back within 2 units of their set points
  4. Hold 10 min: suction 29–31 barg, TI-109 ≤ 130 °C, flare < 1 t/h

Part 8 · graded procedure

Hot afternoon: take 10 % more gas without flaring

Objective. Make room for 10 % more gas on a hot afternoon by cutting the power needed per tonne, then take it without flaring.
Situation. Ambient is heading for 40 °C and production control wants to send 10 % more gas. The gas turbine has little margin. Reduce the power needed per tonne before the extra gas arrives.
Start: lined out at designTime limit: 1 h 30 mingraded on the tracker

Tracker steps

  1. TIC-106 set point lowered to 36 °C or less (less section 2 work)
  2. PIC-101 set point raised to 30.5–31.0 barg (lower overall ratio)
  3. Export FI-114 ≥ 208 MMSCFD
  4. Hold 10 min: flare < 1 t/h, TI-109 ≤ 130 °C, LIC-107 ≤ 65 %, margins ≥ 7 %

Part 8 · graded procedure

Optimisation: stop wasting fuel (live, 60 min)

Objective. Find and correct the settings that waste fuel within 60 minutes, with no alarms standing.
Situation. After a maintenance job the day shift left UV-103 open by hand, the intercooler set point high and the suction set point low. The GT burns too much fuel. Put it right.
Start: lined out at designTime limit: 1 hgraded live

Tracker steps

  1. UIC-103 and UIC-108 in AUTO with both recycle valves ≤ 2 %
  2. Fuel FI-100 ≤ 5.05 t/h (design 4.97)
  3. PIC-101 29.8–30.5 barg and TIC-106 38–42 °C
  4. No alarm active or unacknowledged

Interactive · the troubleshooting method

Think EQUIPPED: six stages for a hidden cause

The method stops you jumping to the first cause that fits: every hypothesis must explain all the readings.

TE-1 · Flare will not go out

Objective. Find where gas is lost while the unit runs normally.
Situation given to you. Night shift reports a steady flare of about 10 t/h although K-100 is running normally at 30 barg suction and no alarm is standing except FI-109.
Start: designMethod: Engage → Define → Explore → Plan → Do it → Look back

Part 8 · what-if

What-if: predict the direction, then let the model answer

Objective. Predict how eight variables move after one event, from the physics of Parts 1–3.

Events

  1. Lower TIC-106 set point 40 → 30 °C
  2. Raise PIC-101 set point 30 → 32 barg
  3. Onshore arrival pressure +15 bar
  4. Production −30 %
  5. Open UV-103 to 40 % by hand
  6. Section 2 fouling

Variables to predict (↑, ↓ or no change after 20 min)

  1. Speed SIC-100
  2. Suction PIC-101
  3. Interstage PI-107
  4. Section 2 outlet TI-109
  5. Shaft power JI-100
  6. Surge margin UIC-103
  7. Export FI-114
  8. Condensate from V-102

Part 8 · summary

What Part 8 settled

  • Seven procedures are graded on safety, order, time and communication.
  • Twenty training exercises start lined out; only the situation is given.

Key Takeaways

1

Read the outlet temperature from the ratio: $T_2=T_1r^{m}$ explains every TI-104 and TI-109 reading.

2

Keep every section right of its control line: speed first, recycle second, never surge.

3

Respect the driver: when GT-100 runs out of power, suction rises and PV-102 flares.

4

After a trip, let the loop settle, vent to header pressure, then restart on full recycle.

5

Use the OTS exercises to practise each skill; state the objective before you start.
